citations.name: requirements.sdk.domain
citations.commentary:
An *application domain* is the application's graph, node contents, and evidence
storage, made available together for criterion execution. In the SDK, it
implements [`Domain`](../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/domain/trait.Domain.html) to supply
its shared types, node and edge operations, and evidence persistence.

rationale:
The commentary cites `requirements.sdk.domain` with `{cite}`, which is the right role for explanatory prose. Its claims agree with the requirement.

- The requirement says every application domain implements `trust_but_verify::domain::Domain`. The commentary says the same.
- The commentary says the trait supplies "shared types, node and edge operations, and evidence persistence". The trait in the requirement matches each part:
  - Shared types: `Error`, `NodeData`, `NodeContent` and `EdgeLabel`.
  - Node and edge operations: `node_path`, `node_content` and `outgoing_edges`.
  - Evidence persistence: `load_evidence` and `store_evidence`.
- The opening phrase is "graph, node contents, and evidence storage, made available together for criterion execution". It is the definition of the term `application_domain`, and it fits the trait's members. The requirement doesn't restate it, and it doesn't contradict the requirement.

The passage doesn't also carry an `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement, so the citation isn't redundant.
